NEW DELHI: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for rain in Delhi-NCR on Thursday, forecasting a generally cloudy sky with spells of rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds. Isolated hailstorms are also likely over Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh on October 29 and 30, according to the weather department.The maximum and minimum temperatures in Delhi are expected to settle at 27 degrees Celsius and 17 degrees Celsius, respectively, on Thursday. The IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall at several places, accompanied by lightning and gusty winds. Wind speeds could reach 40-50 kmph during the morning, while winds of 30-40 kmph are likely during the rest of the day.The unsettled weather is expected to continue on Friday, with the IMD forecasting thunderstorms accompanied by rain. Conditions are likely to remain cloudy as the weather system brings a spell of rainfall to the national capital and adjoining areas.The IMD's latest warning for Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh also flags the possibility of hailstorms on Thursday and Friday. Residents have been advised to remain cautious during thunderstorms and strong winds.

Parts of Delhi received rain on Thursday (October 29) morning, and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for light rainfall, lightning and thunderstorms through the day.
The IMD said, “Generally cloudy sky. A spell of very light to light rain with moderate rain accompanied with thunderstorm/lightning and strong surface winds reaching 30-40 kmph during morning/forenoon. Another spell of very light to light rain with moderate rain accompanied with thunderstorm/lightning during the afternoon/evening.”
Meanwhile, several other states/UTs are likely to witness heavy rainfall following the landfall of Severe Cyclonic Storm “Arnab" near Andhra Pradesh on October 28. "Latest observations indicate that the landfall process completed with the central region moving completely into land by 0800 hrs IST," the IMD said.
Now, the cyclone is very likely to move north-northwestwards during the next 48 hours and weaken gradually. “It will weaken into a Cyclonic Storm during the next 06 hours and further into a Deep Depression during the subsequent 06 hours,” the IMD said in a weather bulletin on Wednesday.

full_text:
Phuket City issues a red alert for Bang Yai Canal as flooding closes Khok Tanot Road in Karon and blocks small vehicles at two Chalong locations.
Phuket City issued a red flood alert on October 29, warning residents along the Bang Yai Canal to move their belongings to higher ground due to rising water levels from heavy rain.
The flooding caused significant traffic disruptions, including the temporary closure of Khok Tanot Road and made several areas in Chalong impassable for small vehicles.
The Thai Meteorological Department forecast thundershowers across 70% of the southern west coast, attributing the persistent heavy rain to a low-pressure area over the Andaman Sea.
Phuket City Municipality issued a red flood alert at 7.40am on October 29, 2026, urging residents and businesses along Bang Yai Canal to move belongings to higher levels as persistent heavy rain and incoming runoff drove up water levels.
The municipality urged people beside the canal to immediately move electrical appliances, valuables and other possessions out of reach of potential flooding. Heavy rain across Phuket, combined with substantial inflows from neighbouring areas, had caused the canal to rise rapidly.
The municipality warned that further sustained rainfall could cause waterlogging and send the canal overflowing into homes. Officials were coordinating with other agencies to monitor vulnerable locations and urged residents to follow official announcements closely.
Khok Tanot Road closed as flooding disrupts Chalong traffic
Karon Municipality temporarily closed Khok Tanot Road after heavy rain caused flooding, citing risks to people and property.
Separate reports identified two locations in Chalong where floodwater prevented small vehicles from passing:
Road outside Wat Tai, formally Wat Latthiwanaram, in Chalong subdistrict, Mueang Phuket district
7.45am: Phuket Info Center reported that floodwater was too deep for small cars and motorcycles to pass.
Khok Tanot traffic-light junction in Chalong
8.10am: Chalong Municipality urged motorists to avoid the junction because small vehicles could not pass through the floodwater.
Chalong Municipality also urged road users to exercise extra caution when travelling.
Thundershowers forecast across 70% of the western South
The Thai Meteorological Department forecast thundershowers across 70% of the southern west coast, with very heavy rain in parts of Phuket. The percentage describes the area expected to experience thundershowers.
The report also cited departmental radar observations showing moderate to very heavy rain across nine southern provinces.
The department attributed the unsettled weather to a low-pressure area over the Andaman Sea and easterly winds across Thailand and the Gulf of Thailand. A high-pressure system, or cool air mass, from China was covering upper Thailand and the South China Sea.
Waves in the Andaman Sea and Gulf of Thailand could exceed two metres in thundershowers. Boat operators were urged to check their routes, navigate cautiously and avoid storm areas. The news report also carried advice for small boats to remain ashore.
Residents needing assistance in Phuket City’s Talat Nuea and Talat Yai subdistricts can contact the municipality’s disaster-prevention service or municipal hotline. Karon Municipality also provides a 24-hour emergency service.
